questions.answer_text: When Xiao Yu got home, she first dried the kitten with a soft towel and gave it some warm milk. Then she made a small bed from an old sweater in a cardboard box. The next morning, the kitten was no longer afraid. It purred happily and followed her around the room, as if it knew it had found a safe home.
questions.explanation: 续写要点分三步：第一，承接上文情节，小雨到家后的动作要合理连贯（擦干、喂奶、安窝），不能突然跳到无关情节；第二，体现小猫的变化（从害怕到安心），形成对比，首尾呼应；第三，题目要求至少一个时间连接词，范文用了 When 和 Then、The next morning，满足要求。注意时态：叙述过去发生的事用一般过去时，purred、followed 等动词形式要一致。
questions.question: 阅读下面短文，根据所给情节进行续写，使之构成一个完整的故事。Xiao Yu found a small wet kitten under a tree on a rainy afternoon. The kitten was cold and hungry, and no one nearby knew who owned it. She decided to take it home in her schoolbag. 续写一段（约50词）：写出小雨回家后如何照顾小猫，以及小猫的变化，至少使用一个表示时间的连接词。
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.answer_text: Lin Tao took a deep breath and decided not to panic. He borrowed a phone from a kind passer-by and called the company to explain that he might be a few minutes late. Then he rode a shared bike to the nearest subway station and arrived just in time. Although he was out of breath, he felt proud that he had stayed calm under pressure.
questions.explanation: 续写要点分三步：第一，情节要解决上文的两个困难（错过公交、手机快没电），范文用借电话说明情况、骑共享单车转地铁，合乎逻辑；第二，心理活动要写出来，decided not to panic 和 felt proud 呼应从紧张到自信的转变；第三，结尾要收束，arrived just in time 与面试时间呼应。注意过去时态和 although 引导的让步状语从句用法。
questions.question: 阅读下面短文，根据所给情节进行续写，使之构成一个完整的故事。Lin Tao missed the early bus on the morning of his first job interview. He ran to the bus stop, but the bus had already left, and his phone battery was almost dead. He still had forty minutes before the interview. 续写一段（约60词）：写出林涛如何想办法按时赶到，并写出他的心理活动。
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.answer_text: "A competition is only one performance, not the whole story," her teacher said gently. She reminded Mei how much her playing had improved since September. Mei wiped her tears and nodded slowly. She realised that progress mattered more than a prize. From that day on, she practised not to beat others, but to enjoy the music itself, and she signed up for the next concert with new confidence.
questions.explanation: 续写要点分三步：第一，老师的话要起安慰和点拨作用，范文用直接引语点明主题，符合题目要求；第二，情感变化要有层次：失落（wiped her tears）→醒悟（realised）→重新出发（signed up），不能只写老师安慰就结束；第三，结尾的决定要与开头失败呼应，形成成长弧线。注意直接引语的标点和 said gently 的位置，以及 practise 与 realised 的过去时。
questions.question: 阅读下面短文，根据所给情节进行续写，使之构成一个完整的故事。Mei failed to win a prize in the school piano competition, although she had practised for three months. She sat alone in the music room, staring at the piano keys, and felt that all her hard work had been wasted. Just then, her teacher came in quietly and sat beside her. 续写一段（约70词）：写出老师说了什么、梅的反应和她之后的决定，要体现情感变化，至少使用一句直接引语。
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 续写第一句要承接上文的犹豫并推动情节。B 项正确：Finally 承接 hesitated，put wallet back、ran over、helped 三个动作解决了老人摔倒的冲突，人物选择符合善良主题。A 项只补充相机背景，不推动情节；C 项介绍商店，与老人摔倒无关；D 项谈不认识路，偏离了是否帮助老人的核心矛盾。
options: A. The camera was very expensive and came from another country.
B. Finally, he put his wallet back into his pocket, ran over, and helped the old man to his feet.
C. The shop sold many kinds of cameras and lenses every day.
D. He had never been to that shop before, so he did not know the way.
questions.question: 阅读下面短文开头，选择最适合作为续写第一句的句子。Chen Lei had saved money for a year to buy a second-hand camera. On the way to the shop, he saw an old man fall down on the wet pavement. The old man could not stand up, and few people stopped to help. Chen Lei hesitated for a moment, thinking about his camera and the closing time of the shop. ______
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.answer_text: Then he took a deep breath, looked at his smiling classmates, and told himself that it was all right to make mistakes.
questions.explanation: 填句要点分三步：第一，位置在紧张之后、开始讲话之前，需要一个转折动作，范文用 took a deep breath 表示平复情绪；第二，要与下句 From that moment 呼应，说明转折点；第三，内容要合理，不能写他突然逃跑或老师替他讲，那样与后文他自己讲话矛盾。时态用一般过去时，与全文一致。
questions.question: 阅读下面短文，在空白处填入一个恰当的过渡句（英文句子），使上下文连贯。Hao had never spoken in public before. His hands shook when the teacher asked him to share his story in front of the class. ______ From that moment, he began to speak slowly, and his voice became steadier with every sentence.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.answer_text: Dear Tom, I'm so glad to hear that you will visit our city next week. I would like to invite you to go hiking with me on Saturday morning. Let's meet at the school gate at 8:00. Please bring comfortable shoes, some water, and a hat, because it may be sunny. I believe we will have a wonderful time together. I'm looking forward to your reply. Yours, Li Hua
questions.explanation: 应用文要点分四步：第一，格式完整，有称呼 Dear Tom 和落款 Yours, Li Hua；第二，邀请目的、时间（Saturday morning, 8:00）、地点（school gate）三要素齐全；第三，准备物品具体且有原因（comfortable shoes, water, hat, because it may be sunny）；第四，语气礼貌友好，用 I would like to invite 和 I'm looking forward to 收尾，符合邀请邮件的规范。
questions.question: 假如你是李华，你的英国朋友 Tom 下周将来你所在的城市参观。请给他写一封电子邮件，邀请他周六上午和你一起去爬山，说明集合时间、地点和需要准备的物品，并表达期待。约60词。写出邮件正文（可含称呼和落款）。
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.answer_text: Notice: Our English Club welcomes new members! We meet every Friday afternoon in Room 301. Activities include an English corner, film dubbing, and speech practice, so you can improve speaking while making friends. If you are interested, please come to Room 205 to find Li Hua, or send an email to our club mailbox before next Wednesday. Come and join us — let's enjoy English together! 提纲：目的（招新）→时间地点（周五下午 Room 301）→内容（英语角/配音/演讲）→报名（Room 205 或邮件，截止下周三）→号召。
questions.explanation: 应用文要点分四步：第一，通知体裁，开头点明招新目的，信息要一目了然；第二，时间、地点、内容、报名方式、截止时间五要素不能缺，范文逐一交代；第三，语言简洁有号召力，Come and join us 符合通知语气；第四，提纲先列要点再成文，避免漏项，这是应用文写作的常用策略。
questions.question: 假如你是学校英语俱乐部负责人李华，请写一则英文招新通知：说明俱乐部每周五下午活动、活动内容（英语角、电影配音、演讲练习）、报名方式（到 Room 205 找李华或发邮件），并号召感兴趣的同学加入。约70词。写出通知正文并给出提纲要点。
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 正式邮件要点：称呼用 Dear + 姓 + 先生称谓，目的用 I am writing to… 委婉说明。B 项完全符合正式、礼貌的要求。A 项 Hey 和 right now 过于随便急促；C 项 Yo 属于俚语口语，不适合师生正式邮件；D 项 I want you to… 是命令语气，缺乏礼貌，不符合应用文得体原则。
options: A. Hey! I need your help right now.
B. Dear Mr. Wang, I am writing to ask for your advice on how to improve my English writing.
C. Yo, teacher, tell me how to study.
D. I want you to solve my problem today.
questions.question: 李华要给老师写一封正式邮件请教学习方法，下列哪句开场白最得体？
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：正式书信中，知道收信人姓名用 Dear Mr./Ms. + 姓开头，结尾用 Yours sincerely；不知道姓名用 Dear Sir/Madam 开头，结尾用 Yours faithfully。题干称呼与结尾搭配正确，因此判断为正确。混淆 sincerely 与 faithfully 的使用条件是常见错误。
questions.question: 判断正误：In a formal English letter, when you know the recipient's name and start with "Dear Mr. Smith,", it is appropriate to end with "Yours sincerely,".
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 这是与过去事实相反的虚拟语气：if 从句用过去完成时 had come，主句用 would have done。B 项完全符合。A 项 came + would enjoy 是与现在事实相反，不合 yesterday 的过去语境；C 项 come + will enjoy 是真实条件句，表示将来可能，不合错过的事实；D 项 have come 不是虚拟语气从句的正确形式，且主句时态不匹配。
options: B. had come; would have enjoyed
questions.question: — I missed the school concert yesterday. — What a pity! If you ______ earlier, you ______ the wonderful violin solo.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 这是 It is/was…that… 强调句型，强调时间状语 only after the rain stopped，结构为 It was + 被强调部分 + that + 其余部分，that 在此不作成分，只起连接作用。B 项正确。A 项 when 会变成时间状语从句，句子缺少强调结构；C 项 which 引导定语从句，需有先行词，不合；D 项 where 引导地点状语从句，与强调时间无关。
questions.question: It was only after the rain stopped ______ the lost dog was found in the small park near the river.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：By the time + 一般过去时，主句表示到过去某时为止已完成的动作，用过去完成时 had done。句中 teacher entered 是过去时间点，finish 发生在它之前，故用 had finished。只写 finished 是一般过去时，不能体现先后；has finished 是现在完成时，与过去语境不符。
questions.question: 用所给动词的正确形式填空：By the time the teacher entered the classroom, most students ______ (finish) their morning reading.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：suggest 表示建议时，其后的 that 从句要用虚拟语气，即 should + 动词原形，should 可省略，即 she go，而不是 she goes。题干用了第三人称单数 goes，违反了虚拟语气规则，因此原句错误，正确形式是 He suggested that she go to the library at once。
questions.question: 判断正误：The sentence "He suggested that she goes to the library at once." is grammatically correct.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：Look! 提示正在进行的动作，用现在进行时 be + doing。B 项 are flying 正确。A 项 fly 是一般现在时，表示习惯，不合正在进行的语境；C 项 flew 是过去时，与 Look! 的现在语境矛盾；D 项 will fly 表示将来，不合眼前正在发生的动作。
questions.question: Look! The children ______ kites happily in the park. Let's join them.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：主语 sports centre 与 build 是被动关系（中心是被建造），且 next year 表示将来，用将来时被动语态 will be + 过去分词。B 项 will be built 正确。A 项 will build 是主动，将来中心自己建造不合逻辑；C 项 builds 是一般现在时主动，且时态不合 next year；D 项 is building 是现在进行时主动，语态和时态都不合。
questions.question: A new sports centre ______ in our town next year, and students will be able to swim there in summer.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：分词作状语表示先后关系：完成作业在检查之前，且逻辑主语 Ming 与 finish 是主动关系，用现在分词完成式 Having finished。C 项正确。A 项 Finish 是动词原形，不能作状语；B 项 Finished 是过去分词，表示被动，与主动关系矛盾；D 项 To finish 表目的，意为为了完成而检查，与先完成再检查的先后顺序不符。
questions.question: ______ his homework carefully, Ming checked every answer once more before handing it in.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：先行词 summer 是时间名词，定语从句中缺少时间状语（in that summer），用关系副词 when 引导。A 项正确。B 项 where 引导地点状语，不合时间先行词；C 项 which 作主语或宾语，从句不缺主宾，不合；D 项 why 引导原因状语，需先行词为 reason，不合。
questions.question: I still remember the summer ______ we spent two weeks learning to swim in the lake near my uncle's house.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：主语从句中缺少主语，且指代事物内容（令我们惊讶的事），用 what 引导，what 兼作从句主语并指代事情。C 项正确。A 项 that 只起连接作用，不作成分，从句 would 缺主语；B 项 which 需有特指范围，不合；D 项 who 指人，从句主语应是事情而非人，不合。
questions.question: ______ surprised us most was that the quiet student gave the best speech in the competition.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：Hardly…when… 结构表示一……就……，hardly 位于句首时主句要部分倒装，即助动词提前；且 hardly…when 中主句动作先发生，用过去完成时。B 项 had he arrived 既倒装又用过去完成时，正确。A 项未倒装；C 项未倒装且时态为一般过去时；D 项 did 倒装但时态不对，不能体现先发生的完成意义。
questions.question: Hardly ______ home when his younger brother asked him to help fix the broken bicycle.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：should have done 表示本应该做而未做，含责备意味，符合你本应早打电话却没打的语境。A 项正确。B 项 must have done 表示对过去的肯定推测（一定做了），与未打电话的事实矛盾；C 项 can have done 不用于肯定句表推测，且语义不合；D 项 may have done 表示可能做了，同样与事实和责备语气不符。
questions.question: You ______ have called me earlier. I was waiting at the station for two hours and could have met you halfway.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：与现在事实相反的虚拟语气，if 从句 be 动词用 were，不论人称和单复数，主句用 would + 动词原形。C 项 were 正确。A 项 am 是真实条件句，不合假设语气；B 项 was 在口语中有时出现，但规范虚拟语气中 be 一律用 were，考试标准答案为 were；D 项 be 原形不能直接作从句谓语。
questions.question: If I ______ you, I would take the morning train instead of waiting until noon.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：否定副词 Never 位于句首时，主句用部分倒装，即助动词 have 提前到主语 I 之前，结构为 Never + have + 主语 + 过去分词。题干句子完全符合该规则，因此判断为正确。未倒装的 Never I have seen… 则是错误的。
questions.question: 判断正误：The sentence "Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset." is grammatically correct, because a negative adverb at the beginning of a sentence causes partial inversion.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：强调句结构为 It is/was + 被强调部分 + that + 句子其余部分。题干强调时间状语 in 2020，去掉 It was…that 后剩余 our family moved to this city 仍是完整句子，结构正确，因此判断为正确。注意 that 在强调句中不作成分，不能换成 when。
questions.question: 判断正误：The sentence "It was in 2020 that our family moved to this city." correctly uses the emphatic pattern It is/was ... that ... to stress the time.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：a/an 的选择取决于后面单词的发音而不是首字母：元音音素开头用 an，辅音音素开头用 a。honest 中的 h 不发音，开头音素是元音 /ɒ/，因此 an honest 是正确的。题干以字母 h 为理由否定 an honest，理由错误，因此整个判断为错误。
questions.question: 判断正误：The expression "an honest student" is wrong, because the word "honest" begins with the letter h.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：固定搭配 be good at + 名词/动名词表示擅长某事，at 后接 drawing 动名词作宾语。填 at 正确。填 in 会变成 be good in…，不表示擅长；填 for 表示目的，不合；填 on 也无此固定搭配。注意 be good at 与 be good for（对……有益）意义不同。
questions.question: 用恰当的介词填空：My younger sister is good ______ drawing, and she often wins prizes in school art shows.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：多音节形容词 interesting 的比较级用 more + 原级，结构为 more interesting than…。题干有 than 提示比较级，且 interesting 为三个音节，不能加 -er。填 more interesting 正确。只填 interesting 是原级，与 than 不搭配；填 most interesting 是最高级，需有 the 和范围，不合。
questions.question: 用括号内形容词的正确形式填空：This science book is ______ (interesting) than the storybook I read last week, so I finished it in two days.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 规则：neither of + 复数名词/代词作主语时，谓语动词用单数形式，因为 neither 表示两者中无一。题干主语是 Neither of the two students，谓语应用第三人称单数 knows。填 know 是复数形式，与 neither 的单数意义冲突；填 knew 时态为过去，与 so 后的一般现在语境和题目要求的形式不符。
questions.question: 用括号内动词的正确形式填空：Neither of the two students ______ (know) the answer to this difficult maths problem, so the teacher explained it again.
questions.subject: yingyu

questions.explanation: 10分度游标卡尺的精确度为1 mm / 10 = 0.1 mm。读数 = 主尺读数 + 对齐格数 × 精确度 = 23 mm + 4 × 0.1 mm = 23.4 mm。注意主尺读数取游标零线左侧最近刻度，不能把对齐格数误当作毫米数直接相加。
questions.question: 用10分度游标卡尺测量一小圆柱的直径，游标零刻度线左侧主尺读数为23 mm，第4条游标刻度线与主尺刻度线对齐。该圆柱的直径是（  ）
questions.subject: wuli

questions.explanation: 螺旋测微器读数 = 固定刻度读数 + 可动刻度读数 × 0.01 mm = 3 mm + 32.0 × 0.01 mm = 3 mm + 0.32 mm = 3.32 mm。题中说明未超过半毫米刻度线，故不加0.5 mm；若可动刻度读数超过50.0才需考虑半毫米线是否露出。
questions.question: 用螺旋测微器测量一金属丝的直径，固定刻度露出3 mm，可动刻度读数为32.0（单位0.01 mm），且未超过半毫米刻度线。该金属丝的直径是（  ）
questions.subject: wuli

questions.explanation: 连续6个计时点之间有5个时间间隔。每个间隔 T = 1 / 50 Hz = 0.02 s，所以总时间 = 5 × 0.02 s = 0.10 s。常见错误是把6个点当成6个间隔，会误得0.12 s。
questions.question: 电磁打点计时器接50 Hz交流电源，相邻两个计时点的时间间隔为0.02 s。某纸带上连续6个计时点之间的时间间隔是______ s。
questions.subject: wuli

questions.explanation: 天平使用前必须先归零游码，再调平衡螺母；若游码不在零位就调平衡，称量结果会系统性偏大。调节时指针左偏则平衡螺母向右调，反之向左调。
questions.question: 用托盘天平测量物体质量前，应先把游码移到标尺左端零刻度处，再调节平衡螺母使横梁平衡。
questions.subject: wuli

questions.answer_text: 外接法；临界电阻约为28.3 Ω，Rx小于临界值，电压表分流影响小于电流表分压影响，故用外接法。
questions.explanation: 临界电阻 R0 = √(Rv × RA) = √(4000 × 0.2) Ω = √800 Ω ≈ 28.3 Ω。Rx = 8 Ω < R0，说明与电压表内阻相比 Rx 很小，电压表分流造成的误差相对较小，而电流表分压的影响相对更大，故选用电流表外接法。内接法适用于 Rx 远大于 R0 的大电阻测量。
questions.question: 用伏安法测一电阻 Rx，Rx 约为 8 Ω，电压表内阻约为 4000 Ω，电流表内阻约为 0.2 Ω。应选用电流表内接法还是外接法？简述判断依据。
questions.subject: wuli

questions.explanation: 用逐差思想：相邻相等时间内的位移差 Δx = aT²。Δx = 3.30 cm − 2.10 cm = 1.20 cm = 0.012 m，T = 0.1 s，所以 a = Δx / T² = 0.012 / 0.01 m/s² = 1.20 m/s²。单位换算时1 cm = 0.01 m，不能直接用厘米数值除以秒平方后不换算。
questions.question: 在“探究小车速度随时间变化的规律”实验中，纸带上相邻计数点时间间隔为0.1 s，连续两段位移分别为2.10 cm和3.30 cm。小车的加速度约为（  ）
questions.subject: wuli

questions.explanation: 竖直方向自由落体：h = (1/2)gt²，得 t = √(2h/g) = √(2×20/10) s = 2 s。水平方向匀速：x = v0t = 10 × 2 m = 20 m。平抛时间只由高度决定，与初速度无关。
questions.question: 一小球以10 m/s的水平初速度从20 m高处平抛，取g = 10 m/s²，不计空气阻力。小球的水平射程是（  ）
questions.subject: wuli

questions.explanation: 位移公式 x = v0t + (1/2)at² = 2×4 m + (1/2)×3×4² m = 8 m + 24 m = 32 m。注意第二项是(1/2)at²，不是at²。
questions.question: 一物体做匀加速直线运动，初速度为2 m/s，加速度为3 m/s²，则它在4 s内的位移是______ m。
questions.subject: wuli

questions.explanation: 由牛顿第二定律 F合 = ma，合力 F合 = 10 N − 4 N = 6 N，所以 a = F合/m = 6/2 m/s² = 3 m/s²。摩擦力方向与拉力相反，合力是两者之差，不是之和。
questions.question: 质量为2 kg的物体在水平面上受到10 N的水平拉力，滑动摩擦力为4 N。物体的加速度大小是（  ）
questions.subject: wuli

questions.explanation: 沿斜面方向合力为重力的分力 mgsinθ，由牛顿第二定律 a = gsinθ = 10 × sin30° m/s² = 10 × 0.5 m/s² = 5 m/s²。初速度为零，2 s内位移 x = (1/2)at² = (1/2)×5×2² m = 10 m。光滑斜面无摩擦力，垂直斜面方向合力为零。
questions.question: 质量为5 kg的物体沿倾角为30°的光滑斜面由静止下滑，取g = 10 m/s²。求物体下滑的加速度大小，以及2 s内的位移大小。
questions.subject: wuli

questions.explanation: 取初速度方向为正，则 v1 = 4 m/s，v2 = −2 m/s。动量变化 Δp = m(v2 − v1) = 0.5 × (−2 − 4) kg·m/s = −3 kg·m/s，大小为3 kg·m/s。动量是矢量，反向弹回时速度取负值，不能用末动量大小减初动量大小得到1 kg·m/s。

questions.explanation: 生长素最主要的生理作用是促进细胞伸长生长。单侧光照射时，胚芽鞘尖端产生的生长素发生横向运输，背光侧生长素分布多、生长快，向光侧生长素分布少、生长慢，胚芽鞘因此向光弯曲生长。生长素的作用具有两重性：低浓度促进生长，高浓度则抑制生长。
questions.question: 促进植物细胞伸长生长、与植物向光性密切相关的激素是________。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 流经生态系统的总能量是指生产者固定的太阳能总量。能量沿食物链逐级传递，具有单向流动、逐级递减的特点，传递效率一般为10%～20%。能量不能像物质那样循环利用，最终都以热能形式散失，因此生态系统需要不断从外界获得能量输入。
questions.question: 生态系统中，生产者通过光合作用固定的太阳能总量是流经该生态系统的________。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 性激素的分级调节是：下丘脑分泌促性腺激素释放激素，作用于垂体，促进垂体分泌促性腺激素，促性腺激素再促进性腺分泌性激素，故A正确。性激素由性腺分泌，而不是垂体或下丘脑直接分泌，故B、D错误。当性激素含量过高时，它会反馈抑制下丘脑和垂体的分泌活动，这种反馈调节维持了激素含量的相对稳定，故C错误。
options: 下丘脑分泌促性腺激素释放激素，促进垂体分泌促性腺激素，进而促进性腺分泌性激素
垂体直接分泌性激素，促进生殖器官的发育
性激素只反馈抑制垂体，对下丘脑没有反馈调节作用
下丘脑直接分泌性激素，调节生殖器官的发育
questions.question: 青春期人体性激素分泌量明显增加。下列关于性激素分级调节的叙述，正确的是？
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 甲状腺激素对下丘脑和垂体存在负反馈调节：甲状腺激素含量升高时抑制TRH和TSH的分泌，含量降低时抑制作用减弱。当甲状腺激素合成不足时，对下丘脑和垂体的反馈抑制减弱，下丘脑分泌的TRH增多，垂体分泌的TSH也增多，TSH进而促进甲状腺的生长和激素分泌，这是一种代偿性调节，故A正确，B、C、D均不符合负反馈减弱的方向。
questions.question: 某患者甲状腺激素合成不足，血液中促甲状腺激素释放激素（TRH）和促甲状腺激素（TSH）的含量变化是？
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 该叙述正确。胰岛素由胰岛B细胞分泌，是人体内唯一能降低血糖的激素：它促进组织细胞加速摄取和利用葡萄糖，促进葡萄糖合成肝糖原和肌糖原，并促进葡萄糖转化为脂肪等非糖物质，从而使血糖浓度下降。与之拮抗的胰高血糖素则促进肝糖原分解和非糖物质转化为葡萄糖，使血糖升高。
questions.question: 胰岛素能促进组织细胞加速摄取、利用和储存葡萄糖，从而降低血糖。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.answer_text: 碘是合成甲状腺激素的原料，缺碘导致甲状腺激素合成不足；甲状腺激素对下丘脑和垂体的反馈抑制作用减弱，下丘脑分泌的促甲状腺激素释放激素和垂体分泌的促甲状腺激素增多；促甲状腺激素持续促进甲状腺细胞增生、腺体肿大，但由于缺碘，甲状腺激素仍合成不足，形成恶性循环。
questions.explanation: 分级调节链条为：下丘脑分泌促甲状腺激素释放激素→垂体分泌促甲状腺激素→甲状腺分泌甲状腺激素。反馈调节为：甲状腺激素含量升高时抑制下丘脑和垂体，含量降低时抑制作用减弱。缺碘时，第一步是原料不足，甲状腺激素合成减少；第二步是负反馈减弱，促甲状腺激素释放激素和促甲状腺激素分泌增多；第三步是促甲状腺激素长期作用，促使甲状腺增生、肿大以代偿，但因缺碘仍不能合成足量激素，所以肿大持续存在。补碘是防治的关键。
questions.question: 某人长期生活在缺碘地区，甲状腺出现肿大（地方性甲状腺肿）。请从分级调节和反馈调节角度解释甲状腺肿大的原因。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.answer_text: 大量出汗使细胞外液渗透压升高，下丘脑渗透压感受器兴奋，下丘脑合成、垂体释放的抗利尿激素增多，促进肾小管和集合管对水的重吸收，尿量减少，细胞外液渗透压逐渐恢复正常。
questions.explanation: 步骤如下：①大量出汗失水多于失盐，细胞外液渗透压升高；②下丘脑中的渗透压感受器感受刺激并产生兴奋；③下丘脑合成抗利尿激素增加，并由垂体释放进入血液；④抗利尿激素作用于肾小管和集合管，增强其对水的重吸收能力；⑤尿量减少，体内水分得以保留，渗透压回落，水平衡恢复。同时机体还会产生渴觉，主动饮水补充水分。
questions.question: 剧烈运动后大量出汗，机体如何通过抗利尿激素调节维持水平衡？简述过程。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 初次免疫时，B细胞增殖分化产生浆细胞和记忆细胞。相同抗原再次入侵时，记忆细胞能迅速增殖分化为大量浆细胞，快速产生大量抗体，因此二次免疫反应更快、更强，潜伏期更短，抗体量更多，故A正确，B、C错误。记忆细胞能特异性识别相同抗原，这正是二次免疫迅速启动的基础，故D错误。
options: 记忆细胞迅速增殖分化，产生抗体更快、更多
二次免疫的潜伏期比初次免疫更长
二次免疫产生的抗体量比初次免疫更少
记忆细胞不能识别再次入侵的相同抗原
questions.question: 关于二次免疫反应的叙述，正确的是？
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 辅助性T细胞在特异性免疫中起枢纽作用：它接受抗原呈递细胞呈递的抗原后被活化，分泌细胞因子，既辅助B细胞活化、增殖分化为浆细胞和记忆细胞（体液免疫），也促进细胞毒性T细胞的增殖分化（细胞免疫）。HIV侵入并破坏辅助性T细胞后，两条特异性免疫途径都会严重受损，机体对病原体的抵抗力大幅下降，易发生机会性感染和肿瘤，故A正确，B、C、D均低估了辅助性T细胞的中心作用。
options: 体液免疫和细胞免疫均会受到严重影响
只有细胞免疫受损，体液免疫不受影响
只有体液免疫受损，细胞免疫不受影响
免疫系统基本不受影响，只是病毒数量增加
questions.question: HIV主要攻击辅助性T细胞。下列推断正确的是？
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 该叙述正确。疫苗通常是减毒、灭活的病原体或其抗原成分，接种后可激发机体的特异性免疫，产生相应的抗体和记忆细胞，但一般不会使人患病。当相同病原体再次入侵时，记忆细胞迅速增殖分化为浆细胞，快速产生大量抗体，免疫反应更快、更强，从而起到预防作用。
questions.question: 接种疫苗后，人体产生的记忆细胞可在相同抗原再次入侵时迅速增殖分化，产生更强的免疫反应。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.answer_text: 自身免疫病是由于免疫系统对自身成分发生免疫反应，产生自身抗体或效应细胞，攻击自身组织器官造成的。免疫缺陷病是免疫功能不足或缺失，机体易受病原体感染；过敏反应是已免疫的机体再次接触无害的外来抗原时发生的过度免疫反应。三者的区别在于免疫异常的方向不同：自身免疫病是攻击自身，免疫缺陷病是防御不足，过敏反应是对无害外来抗原反应过强。
questions.explanation: 机理：正常情况下免疫系统能区分“自己”和“非己”，对自身成分具有耐受性；当这种耐受被打破时，免疫系统把自身组织当作抗原攻击，产生自身抗体，引起组织损伤，如系统性红斑狼疮、类风湿性关节炎。区别：①免疫缺陷病是免疫系统功能低下，如先天缺乏某种免疫细胞或艾滋病导致辅助性T细胞大量减少，表现为反复感染；②过敏反应是机体对花粉、食物等本来无害的外来抗原反应过度，且一般发生在已免疫机体再次接触过敏原时，表现为发作迅速、消退较快；③自身免疫病攻击对象是自身，病程常迁延反复。
questions.question: 系统性红斑狼疮属于自身免疫病。请简述自身免疫病的发病机理，并说明它与免疫缺陷病、过敏反应的主要区别。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 标志重捕法的计算公式为：种群数量N＝第一次捕获并标记数×第二次捕获数÷第二次捕获中有标记数。代入数据：N＝40×50÷8＝250条，故B正确。该方法成立的前提是：种群封闭、标记物不影响被标记个体的生存和活动、标记个体与未标记个体被重捕的概率相等。200条、320条、400条均不是按公式计算的结果。
questions.question: 某湖泊调查鲫鱼种群数量：第一次捕获40条，标记后放回；第二次捕获50条，其中有标记的8条。按标志重捕法估算，该湖泊鲫鱼种群数量约为？
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 豆科植物为根瘤菌提供有机物，根瘤菌为豆科植物提供氮素，双方互利，故A正确。狼捕食羊，二者是捕食关系，不是竞争关系，故B错误。菟丝子从大豆体内吸取营养，对大豆有害而自身获利，属于寄生关系，故C错误。两种草履虫混合培养时一方消失，说明二者争夺共同资源，属于竞争关系，竞争的结果常是一方占优势、另一方被淘汰，故D错误。
options: 豆科植物与根瘤菌是互利共生关系
菟丝子与大豆是捕食关系
两种草履虫混合培养，一种消失、另一种增多，说明二者为互利共生关系
questions.question: 下列关于种间关系的叙述，正确的是？
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 样方法的关键是随机取样：样方的位置不能由调查者主观挑选，而应通过随机方法确定，同时样方数量要足够、大小要适宜，这样才能使调查结果接近真实值，减小误差。若只在植株密集处取样，会高估种群密度；只在稀疏处取样则会低估。计数时还要注意样方边缘个体的计数原则，一般计上不计下、计左不计右。
questions.question: 用样方法调查植物种群密度时，取样的关键是________，以避免主观偏差。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.answer_text: 弃耕农田原有土壤条件基本保留，土壤中还保留着植物的种子和其他繁殖体，不是从裸岩等无生命起点开始的演替，因此属于次生演替。演替过程中物种丰富度逐渐增大，群落结构趋于复杂，垂直分层和水平镶嵌现象越来越明显。
questions.explanation: 区分依据：初生演替发生在从未有过植被或原有植被被彻底消灭的地方，如裸岩、沙丘；次生演替发生在原有植被虽已不存在，但原有土壤条件基本保留，甚至还保留着植物的种子或其他繁殖体的地方，弃耕农田符合后者。变化趋势：随着演替进行，能适应环境的物种不断迁入、定居，物种丰富度增大；不同物种在空间上分层分布和镶嵌分布越来越明显，群落结构由简单趋向复杂，群落的稳定性也逐渐提高。
questions.question: 弃耕农田上发生的群落演替属于次生演替。请说明理由，并简述该演替过程中物种丰富度和群落结构的变化趋势。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: PCR的每次循环包括变性、复性和延伸三步：变性时在90℃以上高温下DNA双链解开，不需要解旋酶；复性时引物与模板链特异性结合；延伸时耐高温的Taq DNA聚合酶在约72℃下合成新链，故B正确，A错误。PCR的原料是四种脱氧核苷酸，不是核糖核苷酸，故C错误。引物必须与模板链上特定的互补序列结合，它决定了扩增片段的起点和特异性，不能任意结合，故D错误。
options: 需要解旋酶将DNA双链解开
高温变性代替了解旋酶的作用，且所用DNA聚合酶耐高温
扩增的原料是核糖核苷酸
引物可以与模板链的任意部位结合
questions.question: PCR扩增目的基因时，下列叙述正确的是？
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 基因工程的基本操作程序依次为：①获取目的基因；②构建基因表达载体，即用限制酶切割目的基因和运载体，再用DNA连接酶把二者连接起来，载体上还应有启动子、终止子、标记基因等；③把基因表达载体导入受体细胞；④目的基因的检测与鉴定。只有先获得目的基因并构建好表达载体，才能导入受体细胞并检测其是否成功表达，因此B正确，A、C、D的顺序均颠倒了关键步骤。
options: 构建基因表达载体→获取目的基因→导入受体细胞→目的基因的检测与鉴定
获取目的基因→构建基因表达载体→导入受体细胞→目的基因的检测与鉴定
获取目的基因→导入受体细胞→构建基因表达载体→目的基因的检测与鉴定
导入受体细胞→获取目的基因→构建基因表达载体→目的基因的检测与鉴定
questions.question: 基因工程的基本操作程序中，正确的顺序是？
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 细胞全能性是指已经分化的细胞仍具有发育成完整个体的潜能，因为每个体细胞都含有一套完整的遗传信息。植物组织培养就是在无菌和人工控制条件下，利用离体组织或细胞，经脱分化形成愈伤组织，再分化形成完整植株的过程，其理论基础正是植物细胞的全能性；培养中生长素与细胞分裂素的比例等条件会影响脱分化和再分化。
questions.question: 植物组织培养的理论基础是植物细胞具有________。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 启动子是位于基因首端的一段特殊DNA序列，是RNA聚合酶识别和结合的部位，能驱动基因的转录。基因表达载体除了目的基因外，还必须含有启动子、终止子、标记基因和复制原点等：启动子保证目的基因能够被转录，终止子保证转录适时停止，标记基因用于筛选含重组载体的受体细胞。没有功能正常的启动子，目的基因即使导入受体细胞也难以高效表达。
questions.question: 在基因工程中，将目的基因与运载体结合后导入受体细胞，若要让目的基因高效表达，常选用含有________（调控元件）的表达载体。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.answer_text: 导入不等于表达，需要确认目的基因是否导入、转录和翻译。分子水平：用DNA分子杂交技术检测目的基因是否导入受体细胞；用分子杂交技术检测目的基因是否转录出mRNA；用抗原—抗体杂交技术检测目的基因是否翻译出蛋白质。个体水平：对转基因生物进行抗虫、抗病等性状鉴定，确认其是否表现出预期性状。
questions.explanation: 必要性：目的基因导入受体细胞的成功率不是100%，而且即使导入了，也可能不转录、不翻译，因此必须逐级验证。分子水平三步对应中心法则的三个环节：①DNA分子杂交，探针与受体细胞DNA结合，证明基因已导入；②分子杂交，探针与mRNA结合，证明基因已转录；③抗原—抗体杂交，抗体与蛋白质结合，证明基因已翻译出蛋白质。个体水平则是最直接的功能验证，如抗虫转基因植物做抗虫接种实验，观察其抗虫效果。只有分子水平和个体水平都通过，才能确认基因工程获得成功。
questions.question: 基因工程中，为什么需要对受体细胞进行目的基因的检测与鉴定？请从分子水平和个体水平分别说明检测方法。
questions.subject: shengwu

questions.explanation: 由勾股定理：AC²=AB²+BC²=3²+4²=9+16=25，所以AC=√25=5。

questions.explanation: 木块做匀速直线运动，处于平衡状态，水平方向上拉力与摩擦力是一对平衡力，大小相等，故摩擦力 f=F=4N，方向与运动方向相反。故选C。

questions.question: 如图所示，小球从20m高处由静止自由下落（g取10m/s²，不计空气阻力），落地时的速度大小为多少？

questions.explanation: 平面镜成像规律：像距等于物距。物距为2m，像距也为2m，像到物体的距离为2m+2m=4m。故选D。

questions.question: 如图所示为锌铜原电池装置（Zn、Cu插入稀硫酸，导线相连），通电工作一段时间后，铜片表面最可能观察到的现象是？
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）Zn比Cu活泼，Zn为负极：Zn－2e-＝Zn2+，Zn溶解；2）Cu为正极，溶液中H+在Cu表面得电子：2H+＋2e-＝H2↑；3）因此Cu本身不溶解、不析出铜，而是有氢气气泡产生。故选C。

questions.question: 如图所示为NaCl晶体的平面示意图（●为Na+，○为Cl-，交替排列），在真实的三维NaCl晶体中，每个Na+周围距离最近的Cl-数目是？

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为用惰性电极电解CuCl2溶液的装置，通电后阳极上产生的物质是？
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）阳极发生氧化反应（失电子）；2）溶液中阴离子有Cl-和OH-，Cl-放电能力强于OH-，优先失电子：2Cl-－2e-＝Cl2↑；3）阴极则是Cu2+得电子析出Cu，H2和O2均不在阳极产生。故选Cl2。

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为N2＋3H2⇌2NH3的速率—时间图象，在t1时刻两条速率曲线同时跃升且v(正)位于v(逆)上方，随后重新走平，则t1时刻改变的条件最可能是？
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）该反应正向是气体分子数减小的放热反应；2）增大压强使正、逆速率都增大，且正反应速率增大更多，平衡正向移动，与图中v(正)＞v(逆)一致；3）升高温度会使v(逆)增幅更大、平衡逆向移动；加入催化剂使两者同等增大、不移动平衡；减小压强则速率下降。故选B。

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为CO2分子的结构示意图（O＝C＝O，直线形），判断：CO2是极性分子。
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）C＝O键本身是极性键；2）但CO2为直线形对称结构，两个C＝O键的极性大小相等、方向相反；3）键的极性相互抵消，分子正负电荷中心重合，因此CO2是非极性分子。题干说法错误，故选错误。

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为实验室制取氢气的装置（锌粒与稀硫酸反应，导管通入倒扣在水槽中的集气瓶），图中所示的收集方法是？
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）图中集气瓶倒扣在水槽中、瓶口向下，气体从水中进入瓶内把水排出；2）这是典型的排水法；3）氢气难溶于水，可用排水法收集；向上、向下排空气法都不用水槽和倒扣集气瓶。故选C。

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为某反应的能量—反应进程图，反应物能量平台高于生成物能量平台，则该反应的ΔH是？
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）ΔH＝生成物总能量－反应物总能量；2）图中反应物平台高于生成物平台，生成物能量减反应物能量为负值；3）能量降低的部分以热的形式放出，属于放热反应。故ΔH小于0，选B。

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为用NaOH溶液滴定盐酸的pH变化曲线，曲线中段陡然上升（突跃），该滴定终点附近溶液的pH最接近？
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）盐酸是强酸、NaOH是强碱，恰好完全中和时生成NaCl溶液；2）NaCl不水解，溶液呈中性，pH＝7；3）图中突跃中点正好对应pH＝7附近，起点pH约1是原盐酸，终点后pH升向13是NaOH过量所致。故选B。

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为某有机物的结构简式（CH3—COOH骨架），该物质所含的官能团是？
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）图中骨架为CH3—C(＝O)—OH，即乙酸；2）—COOH由羰基和羟基组合而成，作为一个整体称为羧基；3）单独的羟基是—OH（乙醇），醛基是—CHO，酯基是—COO—，均不符合。故选羧基。

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为氢氧燃料电池示意图，左侧通入H2，右侧通入O2，则通入H2的一极是？
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）燃料电池中燃料在负极发生氧化反应：H2－2e-＝2H+（或在碱性条件下生成水）；2）氧化剂O2在正极发生还原反应得电子；3）因此通H2的一极失电子，是负极。故选B。

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为同一反应的两条能量—反应进程曲线，其中较低峰的曲线标注为“加催化剂”，关于催化剂作用的正确描述是？
options: 降低活化能，且不改变反应的ΔH
升高活化能，且不改变反应的ΔH
降低活化能，同时改变反应的ΔH
不改变活化能，只改变反应的ΔH
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）图中两条曲线起点（反应物）和终点（生成物）能量相同，所以ΔH不变；2）加催化剂的曲线峰更低，即活化能降低；3）活化能降低使更多分子达到活化状态、速率加快，但不改变平衡和ΔH。故选A。

questions.subject: huaxue
questions.question: 如图所示为过滤装置（漏斗、滤纸、烧杯），过滤结束后，滤渣与滤液的去向正确的是？
options: 滤渣留在滤纸上，滤液进入烧杯
滤渣进入烧杯，滤液留在滤纸上
滤渣和滤液都留在滤纸上
滤渣和滤液都进入烧杯
questions.explanation: 步骤：1）过滤利用滤纸孔隙：液体和小颗粒可透过滤纸，难溶固体颗粒大于孔隙被截留；2）因此滤渣留在滤纸上；3）透过的液体称为滤液，沿漏斗颈流入下方烧杯。故选A。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示的植物细胞中,能进行光合作用的细胞器是下列哪一项?
questions.explanation: 第一步:图中标注的②是扁平椭圆形的绿色结构,即叶绿体。第二步:叶绿体含有叶绿素,是植物进行光合作用的场所,光反应在类囊体薄膜上进行,暗反应在叶绿体基质中进行。第三步:线粒体是有氧呼吸的主要场所,液泡主要调节渗透压和储存物质,细胞核是遗传和代谢的控制中心,均不能进行光合作用。故选叶绿体。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示曲线中,某物质的运输速率随氧气浓度增大而增大,达到一定值后趋于稳定。据此判断,该物质的运输方式最可能是下列哪一项?
questions.explanation: 第一步:氧气浓度影响细胞呼吸供能,运输速率随氧气浓度增大而增大,说明该运输需要消耗能量。第二步:自由扩散和协助扩散都不消耗能量,速率不应随氧气浓度这样变化,可排除。第三步:速率最终趋于稳定,说明载体蛋白数量有限,达到饱和。第四步:既需能量又需载体的是主动运输,胞吐虽耗能但不表现为这种载体饱和曲线。故选主动运输。

questions.image_alt: 坐标曲线图,横轴为氧气浓度,纵轴为运输速率,曲线先上升后趋于水平

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示为某植物净光合速率随光照强度变化的曲线,图中B点表示下列哪一项?
options: 呼吸速率最大时的光照强度
光合速率最大时的光照强度
questions.explanation: 第一步:纵轴为净光合速率,净光合速率=总光合速率-呼吸速率。第二步:光照为零时曲线在横轴下方,说明此时只有呼吸作用,净光合速率为负。第三步:B点处净光合速率为零,说明此时光合作用固定的二氧化碳量恰好等于呼吸作用释放的二氧化碳量,即光合速率等于呼吸速率。第四步:这一光照强度称为光补偿点;C点之后不再上升才是光饱和点。故选光补偿点。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示为温度对某植物细胞呼吸速率的影响曲线。超过最适温度后呼吸速率下降,最主要的原因是下列哪一项?
options: 呼吸作用有关的酶活性降低甚至失活
底物葡萄糖被完全耗尽
questions.explanation: 第一步:曲线先随温度升高而上升,说明在一定范围内温度升高使酶活性增强,呼吸速率加快。第二步:超过最适温度后曲线下降,这是酶促反应的典型特征。第三步:高温会破坏酶的空间结构,使酶活性降低甚至失活,呼吸作用随之减弱。第四步:题干并未说明底物或氧气耗尽,线粒体也不会因温度略升而全部消失。故选酶活性降低甚至失活。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示细胞中,染色体整齐地排列在赤道板上。该细胞处于有丝分裂的哪个时期,染色体数目是多少?
questions.explanation: 第一步:判断时期:染色体的着丝粒整齐排列在细胞中央的赤道板上,这是有丝分裂中期的典型特征;前期染色体散乱分布,后期着丝粒分裂、染色体移向两极。第二步:数染色体:图中细胞中央有4条形态清晰的染色体。第三步:中期染色体数目与体细胞相同,尚未因着丝粒分裂而加倍,所以是4条,不是8条。故选中期、4条。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示为基因型为Aa的豌豆自交的遗传图解。子代中表现为显性性状的个体所占的比例是下列哪一项?
questions.explanation: 第一步:亲本均为Aa,各产生A和a两种配子,比例各为1/2。第二步:按棋盘法组合:AA占1/4,Aa占1/2,aa占1/4,基因型比例为1:2:1。第三步:A对a为完全显性,AA和Aa都表现为显性性状,合计1/4+1/2=3/4。第四步:只有aa表现为隐性性状,占1/4。故显性性状个体占3/4。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示系谱中,Ⅰ-1和Ⅰ-2表现正常,Ⅱ-1和Ⅱ-2均患病。该遗传病最可能的遗传方式是下列哪一项?
questions.explanation: 第一步:判断显隐性:父母Ⅰ-1、Ⅰ-2均正常,子女中出现患者,符合无中生有,故为隐性遗传,排除显性选项。第二步:判断常染色体还是伴X:Ⅱ-2为患病女儿,若为伴X隐性遗传,患病女儿的两个致病基因一个来自父亲,则父亲Ⅰ-1必为患者,但Ⅰ-1表现正常,矛盾。第三步:因此该病不可能是伴X隐性遗传,只能是常染色体隐性遗传。第四步:常染色体隐性遗传中,父母均为携带者Aa,子女患病概率为1/4,与系谱相符。故选常染色体隐性遗传。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示为遗传信息的传递过程,其中翻译过程发生的场所是下列哪一项?
questions.explanation: 第一步:图中DNA通过转录形成mRNA,转录主要在细胞核中进行。第二步:mRNA离开细胞核,与图中的核糖体结合,以mRNA为模板、以氨基酸为原料合成蛋白质,这个过程就是翻译。第三步:线粒体是供能场所,高尔基体主要对蛋白质进行加工、分类和包装,都不是翻译的场所。故翻译的场所是核糖体。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示反射弧的五个部分中,兴奋传导的正确顺序是下列哪一项?
options: 感受器→传入神经→神经中枢→传出神经→效应器
感受器→传出神经→神经中枢→传入神经→效应器
效应器→传入神经→神经中枢→传出神经→感受器
神经中枢→感受器→传入神经→传出神经→效应器
questions.explanation: 第一步:反射弧由感受器、传入神经、神经中枢、传出神经和效应器五部分组成。第二步:刺激首先被感受器接受,产生兴奋。第三步:兴奋沿传入神经传到神经中枢,经分析综合后,沿传出神经传到效应器,引起反应。第四步:兴奋在反射弧中只能单向传导,顺序不可颠倒,效应器是终点而非起点。故正确顺序为感受器→传入神经→神经中枢→传出神经→效应器。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示为神经纤维受刺激后膜电位的变化曲线。图中b点膜电位由负变正并达到峰值,形成的主要原因是下列哪一项?
questions.explanation: 第一步:a段为静息电位,膜内为负、膜外为正,主要由钾离子外流维持。第二步:受刺激后,膜上钠离子通道开放,钠离子顺浓度梯度大量内流。第三步:钠离子内流使膜内电位迅速升高,由负变正,形成动作电位的上升支,到达b点峰值。第四步:随后钠离子通道关闭、钾离子外流使电位恢复,故b点峰值的形成原因是钠离子内流,而非钾离子外流。故选钠离子大量内流。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示为某人进食后血糖浓度的变化曲线。进食后0~1小时血糖升高,此时胰岛素的分泌量变化及其作用是下列哪一项?
options: 分泌减少,促进血糖升高
分泌减少,促进血糖降低
分泌增加,促进血糖升高
分泌增加,促进血糖降低
questions.explanation: 第一步:进食后食物中的糖类被消化吸收,血糖浓度在0~1小时内升高。第二步:血糖升高会刺激胰岛B细胞,使胰岛素分泌量增加。第三步:胰岛素能促进组织细胞加速摄取、利用和储存葡萄糖,抑制肝糖原分解和非糖物质转化,从而使血糖浓度降低。第四步:血糖回落后胰岛素分泌随之减少,维持血糖平衡。故选分泌增加、促进血糖降低。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示为体液免疫的部分过程,其中能够产生抗体的细胞是下列哪一项?
questions.explanation: 第一步:抗原经吞噬细胞处理后呈递给T细胞,T细胞再将抗原呈递给B细胞。第二步:B细胞接受刺激后增殖分化,一部分形成记忆细胞,另一部分形成浆细胞。第三步:只有浆细胞能够合成并分泌抗体,抗体与抗原特异性结合,发挥免疫作用。第四步:B细胞本身不直接分泌抗体,吞噬细胞和T细胞也不产生抗体。故选浆细胞。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示食物网中,鹰所处的营养级是下列哪一级?
questions.explanation: 第一步:数营养级时从生产者算起:草为第一营养级。第二步:图中食物链为草→鼠→蛇→鹰:鼠以草为食,为第二营养级;蛇以鼠为食,为第三营养级。第三步:鹰以蛇为食,处于该食物链的第四个环节,因此为第四营养级。第四步:另一条链草→兔→狐不含鹰,不影响鹰的营养级判断。故选第四营养级。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示为种群数量的S形增长曲线,虚线表示环境容纳量K。种群增长速率最大时,种群数量约为下列哪一项?
questions.explanation: 第一步:S形曲线中,种群数量先加速增长,后减速增长,最终在K值附近波动。第二步:增长速率在曲线的拐点处最大,该拐点对应的种群数量约为K/2。第三步:当种群数量小于K/2时,资源相对充足,增长速率随数量增加而加快;超过K/2后,环境阻力增大,增长速率下降。第四步:到达K时增长速率为零,种群数量不再增长。故增长速率最大时约为K/2。

questions.image_alt: S形增长曲线图,种群数量先慢后快再趋平,虚线标出K和K/2

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示的碳循环中,分解者能将动植物遗体中的有机物分解为无机物归还无机环境。这一说法是否正确?
questions.explanation: 第一步:图中动植物遗体指向分解者,分解者再指向大气中的二氧化碳,构成一条完整的归还路径。第二步:分解者(如细菌、真菌)通过分解作用,将动植物遗体和排泄物中的有机物分解为二氧化碳、水和无机盐等无机物。第三步:这些无机物归还到无机环境后,可再次被绿色植物通过光合作用利用,完成物质循环。第四步:因此题干说法符合碳循环的原理,判断为正确。

questions.subject: shengwu
questions.question: 如图所示食物链中,生产者是哪种生物?请填写该生物的名称。
questions.explanation: 第一步:生产者是指能够利用光能或化学能将无机物合成为有机物的生物,主要是绿色植物。第二步:图中食物链为草→兔→狐,草位于食物链的起点,能够进行光合作用制造有机物。第三步:兔以草为食,是初级消费者;狐以兔为食,是次级消费者,二者都不能自己制造有机物。第四步:因此该食物链的生产者是草。

questions.subject: yingyu
questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history of libraries in small towns.
Why small town libraries are losing their funding.
How to repair an old building with a leaking roof.
How a town library was saved and run by local residents.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：第一步，通读全文把握主线——图书馆失去经费后并未关闭，而是由居民自己打理并越办越好。第二步，排除干扰项：B 只提到了开头失去经费的原因，不是全文重点；C 只提到了修屋顶这一个细节；A 过于宽泛，文中没有讲小镇图书馆的历史。第三步，D 覆盖了全文核心：居民接管、选书、开课、雪天开放等，全部围绕“居民拯救并运营图书馆”展开，因此选 D。
questions.passage:
When the small town library in Maplewood lost its funding three years ago, most people expected it to close. The building was old, the roof leaked, and there were only two part-time librarians left. Instead of giving up, a group of local residents decided to run the library themselves. They cleaned the rooms, repaired the shelves, and took turns staffing the front desk. Within a year, the library was open six days a week, longer than before.

What makes Maplewood Library different is not just who works there, but how its books are chosen. Every month, readers suggest titles they would like to see on the shelves, and volunteers vote on which ones to buy with the money raised from book sales and small donations. A retired teacher, Mrs. Ellis, keeps a notebook of requests from children, while a group of teenagers runs a reading club every Friday afternoon. The club started with five members and now has more than forty.

The library has also become a place for learning new skills. On Saturday mornings, volunteers offer free classes in computer use, job applications, and English conversation. Local farmers bring fresh produce to share after the classes, and people stay to talk. "I used to come here only to borrow books," says Mr. Chen, a regular visitor. "Now I come because this is where I meet my neighbours."

Last winter, when heavy snow closed the roads for three days, the library stayed open as a warming centre. Volunteers brought blankets and hot drinks, and neighbours checked on elderly residents who lived alone. The town council, which had once planned to sell the building, has now agreed to pay for the roof repairs. The library's future is still not certain, but its supporters say the lesson is clear: a library is not just a building full of books. It is a place that belongs to the people who use it, and when people take responsibility for it, it can survive even the hardest times.
questions.passage_title: A Library Run by Its Readers

questions.subject: yingyu
questions.question: According to the passage, how are new books chosen at Maplewood Library?
options: The town council decides which books to buy.
The two part-time librarians choose all the books.
Readers suggest titles and volunteers vote on them.
Children write to publishers to ask for free books.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到第二段原句——每月读者提议书名，志愿者投票决定用筹款买哪些。第一步，A 与文意相反，镇议会曾想卖掉大楼，并未选书；第二步，B 与事实不符，文中说只剩两名兼职馆员，但选书是读者提议加志愿者投票；第三步，D 是编造，文中只说退休教师记录儿童的请求，并非向出版社要免费书。因此选 C。

questions.question: What can we learn about the Friday reading club?
options: It was started by Mrs. Ellis alone.
It meets only during the winter.
It has grown from five members to over forty.
It is only open to teenagers.

questions.question: The underlined word "supporters" in the last paragraph most probably means ______.

people who donate money to the library
people who back and help the library
people who borrow books from the library

questions.question: What can be inferred from the passage?

The town council has always supported the library.

questions.subject: yingyu
questions.question: What is the main purpose of the rooftop farm described in the passage?
options: To produce as much honey as possible for sale.
To make the office building look more attractive.
To provide a home and food for city bees.
To attract tourists to the city.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：第一步，抓住项目起源——Lena 发现城市蜜蜂难觅食物，于是提议在屋顶种花、放蜂箱。第二步，A 只是副产品，文中说蜂蜜收入用于买更多植物，并非主要目的；第三步，B 没有依据，文中没有说为了美观；第四步，D 是编造，文中说的是学校带孩子参观学习授粉，而非吸引游客。因此选 C。
questions.passage:
From the street, the building looks like any other office block in the city: glass walls, grey concrete, and a row of bicycles outside. Go up to the roof, however, and you will find something unexpected — twelve beehives, rows of flowering plants, and, on warm days, thousands of bees moving busily between them. The rooftop farm belongs to a small company that decided, five years ago, to turn its unused roof into a home for bees.

The idea came from one of the company's workers, Lena, who kept bees as a hobby in the countryside. She noticed that city bees often struggled to find food because there were few flowers and too many paved surfaces. She suggested planting flowers on the roof and placing hives there. At first, her colleagues laughed. They worried that the bees would sting people or fly into the offices. Lena patiently explained that honeybees are usually calm when they are not disturbed, and that the hives would be placed far from the doors and windows.

To everyone's surprise, the project worked. The bees produced honey, which the company now sells in small jars, and the money is used to buy more plants. More importantly, the rooftop garden has attracted butterflies and other insects, and workers say they feel calmer when they spend their lunch breaks among the flowers. Some nearby buildings have started similar projects, and local schools now bring children to visit the roof and learn about pollination.

Not everyone is convinced, however. Some residents worry about safety, and the company has had to spend money on protective nets and regular checks by a professional beekeeper. Lena admits that rooftop beekeeping is not a solution to all the problems facing bees, such as the loss of wildflower meadows and the use of harmful chemicals on farms. But she believes it is a good start. "If every city building used its roof this way," she says, "bees would have more food, and people would have a closer connection with nature."
questions.passage_title: Bees on the Rooftop

questions.subject: yingyu
questions.question: Why did Lena's colleagues laugh at first?
options: They thought honey could not be sold in the city.
They did not believe Lena knew anything about bees.
They wanted to use the roof for a car park.
They thought bees would be dangerous to people in the building.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到第三段——同事担心蜜蜂会蜇人或飞进办公室。第一步，B 无依据，文中没有质疑 Lena 的养蜂经验；第二步，C 是编造，文中没有提到停车场；第三步，A 与文意无关，同事的担心是安全问题，不是销售问题。因此选 D。

From the street, the building looks like any other office block in the city: glass walls, grey concrete, and a row of bicycles outside. Go up to the roof, however, and you will find something unexpected — twelve beehives, rows of flowering plants, and, on warm days, thousands of bees moving busily between them. The rooftop farm belongs to a small company that decided, five years ago, to turn its unused roof into a home for bees.

The idea came from one of the company's workers, Lena, who kept bees as a hobby in the countryside. She noticed that city bees often struggled to find food because there were few flowers and too many paved surfaces. She suggested planting flowers on the roof and placing hives there. At first, her colleagues laughed. They worried that the bees would sting people or fly into the offices. Lena patiently explained that honeybees are usually calm when they are not disturbed, and that the hives would be placed far from the doors and windows.

To everyone's surprise, the project worked. The bees produced honey, which the company now sells in small jars, and the money is used to buy more plants. More importantly, the rooftop garden has attracted butterflies and other insects, and workers say they feel calmer when they spend their lunch breaks among the flowers. Some nearby buildings have started similar projects, and local schools now bring children to visit the roof and learn about pollination.

Not everyone is convinced, however. Some residents worry about safety, and the company has had to spend money on protective nets and regular checks by a professional beekeeper. Lena admits that rooftop beekeeping is not a solution to all the problems facing bees, such as the loss of wildflower meadows and the use of harmful chemicals on farms. But she believes it is a good start. "If every city building used its roof this way," she says, "bees would have more food, and people would have a closer connection with nature."

questions.passage:
When Amina was fifteen, her family moved to a village where cooking still meant collecting firewood every day. The smoke from the fires made her grandmother cough, and the walk to gather wood took hours that could have been spent studying. Amina had learned about solar energy at school, and she wondered whether sunlight could do the cooking instead.

With help from her science teacher, Amina built her first solar cooker from a cardboard box, aluminium foil, and a sheet of glass. The cooker worked, but only on very sunny days, and it took a long time to heat food. Instead of giving up, she kept a notebook of every test: the angle of the box, the time of day, the type of food, and how long it took to cook. After more than fifty tests, she changed the shape of the reflector and added a dark pot to absorb more heat. The new version could boil water in about forty minutes.

News of the cooker spread through the village. At first, some neighbours were doubtful. They said the food would taste strange or the cooker would break easily. Amina invited them to watch her cook rice and vegetables, and to taste the food themselves. Gradually, more families asked her to help them build one. Amina did not charge for her help. Instead, she asked each family to teach another family how to use the cooker, so that the knowledge would spread.

Today, Amina is studying engineering at university, but she still returns to the village during holidays to improve the design. Her latest cooker uses recycled materials and can be folded flat for easy carrying. She says the most important lesson she learned was not about solar energy, but about patience. "A good idea is only the beginning," she says. "You have to test it, listen to people, and keep improving it. That is how a small school project can change everyday life."

questions.passage:
Three years ago, a group of high school students in a coastal town decided to spend one Saturday cleaning their local beach. They expected to collect a few bags of rubbish. Instead, they filled more than eighty bags in a single morning, most of them with plastic bottles, bags, and fishing nets. The students were shocked, but they also noticed something useful: most of the rubbish came from a few specific places, such as the river mouth and the car park near the beach.

One of the students, Daniel, suggested recording where each bag of rubbish was found, so that the town could understand the problem better. At first, they used a paper map and coloured pens. Soon, however, Daniel built a simple phone app that allowed volunteers to photograph rubbish, mark its location, and record its type. The app was free, and within six months, volunteers in twelve other towns were using it.

The data collected by the app surprised local officials. It showed that nearly half of the beach rubbish came from the river, which carried waste from inland areas. As a result, the town installed new bins along the river and started a campaign to stop people from throwing rubbish into drains. The following year, the amount of rubbish on the beach fell by almost a third. The students had not only cleaned a beach; they had helped change how their town dealt with waste.

Daniel is careful not to claim too much. He points out that the app cannot clean beaches by itself, and that plastic waste is a global problem that needs bigger changes in how products are made and used. But he believes that small, local actions matter. "When people can see the problem on a map," he says, "it stops being someone else's problem. It becomes our problem, and then we start to fix it."

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a grandfather and granddaughter combine traditional paper-cutting with modern product design.
How to cut paper flowers and birds by hand.
Why young people do not like traditional art.
The history of paper-cutting in Hangzhou.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：第一步，通读全文——主线是周师傅与孙女 Lin 合作，把传统剪纸图案用在手机壳、笔记本、灯具等日常产品上，并开设周末课程。第二步，B 只是一个细节（游客先学剪一朵简单的花）；第三步，C 与事实相反，文中说年轻买家反馈积极，很多人因此想了解剪纸；第四步，D 过于宽泛，文中没有系统讲剪纸历史。因此选 A。
questions.passage:
In a small workshop in Hangzhou, 62-year-old paper-cutting artist Master Zhou works beside his granddaughter, Lin, who is studying product design at university. On the table are two very different things: Master's traditional red paper cuttings of flowers and birds, and Lin's laptop, on which she is turning those same patterns into designs for phone cases, notebooks, and lamps. Their cooperation began three years ago, when Lin suggested that old patterns could reach young people if they appeared on everyday objects.

At first, Master Zhou was not sure. He worried that putting paper-cutting patterns on products would make the art less serious, or that people would buy the products without understanding the skill behind them. Lin listened carefully and changed her approach. Instead of simply copying the patterns, she invited her grandfather to teach her the cutting techniques, and she added a small card to each product explaining the meaning of the pattern and how it was made. Sales grew slowly, but the feedback from young buyers was encouraging: many said they had never thought about paper-cutting before, and now they wanted to learn more.

The workshop now runs weekend classes, where Master Zhou teaches cutting and Lin teaches design. Visitors first learn to cut a simple flower, and then try turning their own design into a product. Master Zhou says he has changed his mind. "I used to think tradition must stay exactly as it was," he says. "Now I think tradition stays alive when young people use it in their own way. The patterns have not changed, but the way people meet them has."

Lin agrees, but she adds a warning. She says that using traditional patterns for products must respect the artists and the culture behind them. Copying a pattern without understanding it, or paying artists too little, would harm the very tradition it claims to celebrate. For their workshop, the rule is simple: the artist is always named, and a fair share of the money goes to the craftspeople who keep the skill alive.

In a small workshop in Hangzhou, 62-year-old paper-cutting artist Master Zhou works beside his granddaughter, Lin, who is studying product design at university. On the table are two very different things: Master's traditional red paper cuttings of flowers and birds, and Lin's laptop, on which she is turning those same patterns into designs for phone cases, notebooks, and lamps. Their cooperation began three years ago, when Lin suggested that old patterns could reach young people if they appeared on everyday objects.

At first, Master Zhou was not sure. He worried that putting paper-cutting patterns on products would make the art less serious, or that people would buy the products without understanding the skill behind them. Lin listened carefully and changed her approach. Instead of simply copying the patterns, she invited her grandfather to teach her the cutting techniques, and she added a small card to each product explaining the meaning of the pattern and how it was made. Sales grew slowly, but the feedback from young buyers was encouraging: many said they had never thought about paper-cutting before, and now they wanted to learn more.

The workshop now runs weekend classes, where Master Zhou teaches cutting and Lin teaches design. Visitors first learn to cut a simple flower, and then try turning their own design into a product. Master Zhou says he has changed his mind. "I used to think tradition must stay exactly as it was," he says. "Now I think tradition stays alive when young people use it in their own way. The patterns have not changed, but the way people meet them has."

Lin agrees, but she adds a warning. She says that using traditional patterns for products must respect the artists and the culture behind them. Copying a pattern without understanding it, or paying artists too little, would harm the very tradition it claims to celebrate. For their workshop, the rule is simple: the artist is always named, and a fair share of the money goes to the craftspeople who keep the skill alive.

options: It started teaching maths only in the afternoon.

questions.passage:
For years, students at Northside High School had to be in class by 7:30 in the morning. Many arrived half asleep, and teachers noticed that first-period lessons were often the least productive of the day. Two years ago, the school tried an experiment: it moved the start time to 8:30. The results, published in a recent school report, have caught the attention of other schools.

According to the report, students slept an average of 45 minutes longer each night after the change. Absences fell by 18 percent, and the number of students arriving late dropped sharply. Test scores in morning subjects, especially maths and science, improved slightly, while afternoon scores stayed about the same. Teachers also reported that students asked more questions in first period and seemed more willing to take part in discussions.

Not everyone welcomed the change, however. Some parents said the later start made it harder to arrange childcare for younger children, or clashed with their own work hours. Bus companies had to change their schedules, which cost extra money. The school's sports teams also had to practise later, which meant some evening matches finished in the dark.

The school's headteacher, Ms. Rivera, says the experiment will continue for another year, but she admits there is no perfect solution. "We have to balance the needs of students, parents, and the wider community," she says. "What the evidence shows is that teenagers' bodies naturally want to sleep later and wake later. If we ignore that, we should not be surprised when they struggle in early morning lessons." Researchers who study sleep agree, but they also warn that a later start alone is not enough. Students still need regular sleep habits, less screen time late at night, and a calm morning routine.
questions.passage_title: Should School Start Later?

options: Taking over all lessons from teachers.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到第二段首句——机器人主要用于数学练习。第一步，A 错误，文中说机器人无法帮助开放性任务，如写故事；第二步，C 与最后一段相反，校方强调机器人是支持教师而非取代；第三步，B 是编造，文中没有提到打扫。因此选 D。
questions.passage:
At a primary school in a small city, a new teaching assistant has joined the staff. It does not eat lunch, never gets tired, and can answer the same question a hundred times without losing patience. It is a robot tutor, about the height of a ten-year-old child, with a friendly face on a screen and wheels that allow it to move between desks.

The robot is used mainly for maths practice. When a pupil gets an answer wrong, the robot does not simply give the correct answer. Instead, it asks a simpler question, gives a hint, and waits for the pupil to try again. Teachers say this approach helps children who are shy about asking for help in front of the whole class. "Some children would rather talk to the robot than raise their hand," says one teacher. "With the robot, there is no fear of looking foolish."

The results so far are mixed. In a six-month trial, pupils who used the robot for twenty minutes a day improved their maths scores more than pupils who did extra worksheets. However, the robot could not help with open-ended tasks, such as writing a story or discussing a moral dilemma. It also sometimes misunderstood children's speech, especially when they spoke quietly or with a strong local accent. In those cases, a human teacher had to step in.

The school's leaders stress that the robot is meant to support teachers, not replace them. They point out that learning is not only about getting the right answer, but also about working with others, asking questions, and understanding feelings — things that a machine cannot truly do. For now, the robot is kept for short practice sessions, while teachers focus on group work, discussion, and creative tasks. The question, the headteacher says, is not whether robots will enter classrooms, but how schools can use them wisely.
questions.passage_title: The Robot Tutor in the Classroom

questions.passage:
At a primary school in a small city, a new teaching assistant has joined the staff. It does not eat lunch, never gets tired, and can answer the same question a hundred times without losing patience. It is a robot tutor, about the height of a ten-year-old child, with a friendly face on a screen and wheels that allow it to move between desks.

The robot is used mainly for maths practice. When a pupil gets an answer wrong, the robot does not simply give the correct answer. Instead, it asks a simpler question, gives a hint, and waits for the pupil to try again. Teachers say this approach helps children who are shy about asking for help in front of the whole class. "Some children would rather talk to the robot than raise their hand," says one teacher. "With the robot, there is no fear of looking foolish."

The results so far are mixed. In a six-month trial, pupils who used the robot for twenty minutes a day improved their maths scores more than pupils who did extra worksheets. However, the robot could not help with open-ended tasks, such as writing a story or discussing a moral dilemma. It also sometimes misunderstood children's speech, especially when they spoke quietly or with a strong local accent. In those cases, a human teacher had to step in.

The school's leaders stress that the robot is meant to support teachers, not replace them. They point out that learning is not only about getting the right answer, but also about working with others, asking questions, and understanding feelings — things that a machine cannot truly do. For now, the robot is kept for short practice sessions, while teachers focus on group work, discussion, and creative tasks. The question, the headteacher says, is not whether robots will enter classrooms, but how schools can use them wisely.

questions.question: Why was the wildlife corridor important?
options: It was the only park in the city.
It allowed animals to move between two large parks to reach food, water, and mates.
It was used by people for walking and cycling.
It was the site of a new road.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到第一段——走廊是动物在两个大公园之间移动的林带，没有它，狐狸、獾和许多鸟会被困在一边，无法到达另一边的食物、水或配偶。第一步，A 错误，走廊连接的是两个公园，并非唯一公园；第二步，C 无依据，文中说的是动物使用；第三步，D 颠倒，新路是切断走廊的东西，而非走廊本身。因此选 B。
questions.passage:
When engineers planned a new road through the northern part of the city, ecologists warned that it would cut through an important wildlife corridor — a strip of woodland that animals used to move between two large parks. Without the corridor, foxes, badgers, and many birds would be trapped on one side, unable to reach food, water, or mates on the other side. The road was still built, but the city agreed to add something unusual: a wide, grass-covered bridge for animals, known as a wildlife overpass.

At first, few animals used the bridge. Cameras showed only the occasional fox crossing at night. The ecologists were patient. They planted native shrubs and grasses on the bridge, added logs for insects to hide under, and kept the bridge free of bright lights. Slowly, more animals began to appear. Within three years, cameras had recorded badgers, deer, hedgehogs, and more than twenty species of birds using the crossing. Even frogs, which might seem unlikely to climb a bridge, were found in the damp soil on its edges.

The success of the overpass has changed how the city plans new roads. Planners now ask ecologists for advice before construction begins, rather than after the damage is done. They also leave gaps in fences and plant trees along roadsides to help smaller animals move safely. Some residents were initially worried that the bridge would bring wild animals too close to their homes, but most now say they enjoy seeing deer in the early morning and hearing birds that had disappeared for years.

The overpass is not a perfect solution. It cost a lot of money, and it cannot help animals that need large, undisturbed areas of wilderness. But for a city that once treated nature as something separate from daily life, it is a sign of change. As one ecologist puts it, "We used to build roads and then wonder where the wildlife went. Now we are learning to build roads that let wildlife stay."
questions.passage_title: A Wildlife Corridor Through the City

options: Because the canteen food was too expensive to buy.
Because large amounts of uneaten food were thrown away, which was costly and bothered students.
Because the canteen staff asked them to cook lunch.
Because they wanted to close the canteen.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到第一段——食堂每天扔掉大量未吃完的食物，浪费昂贵，也让学过饥饿与气候变化的学生感到困扰。第一步，A 偷换概念，昂贵的是浪费本身，不是饭价；第二步，C、D 均是编造，文中没有说让学生做饭或关闭食堂。因此选 B。
questions.passage:
Every day, the canteen at Riverside School threw away large amounts of uneaten food. Cooks prepared meals based on guesswork, and students often took more than they could eat. The waste was expensive, and it bothered many students who had learned about hunger and climate change in class. Last year, a group of students decided to do something about it, with help from the canteen staff.

Their first step was simple: for two weeks, they weighed all the food thrown away each day and recorded what it was. The results were clear. Rice and vegetables were wasted most, especially on days when the menu included a dish that students did not like. Armed with this data, the students suggested smaller portion sizes, a choice of two main dishes instead of one, and a system that allowed students to take a smaller first helping and come back for more if they were still hungry.

The canteen staff agreed to try the plan for a month. The results were encouraging. Food waste fell by 40 percent, and the money saved was used to buy fresher ingredients. Students also reported that they enjoyed lunch more, because they could choose food they actually wanted. One unexpected benefit was that the kitchen staff, who had once felt blamed for the waste, now felt part of the solution. They began suggesting their own ideas, such as using leftover vegetables in soup the next day.

Not all problems are solved. On busy days, queues are still long, and some students still take too much food. But the school now publishes its waste figures every month, so everyone can see the progress. The students who started the project say the key lesson is that waste is not just a kitchen problem. "When we measured it, we could see it," one student says. "And when we could see it, we could change it."
questions.passage_title: The School Canteen That Wastes Less

questions.question: Why did Jia feel angry and lonely after the accident?
options: Because her parents did not allow her to watch sports.
Because she watched classmates play sports from the sidelines while she could not run.
Because she did not like her classmates.
Because doctors told her to leave school.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到第一段——几个月里，她在场边看着同学运动，感到愤怒和孤独。第一步，A 无依据，文中没有说父母不让她看；第二步，C 是编造，文中说同学后来还为她加油；第三步，D 错误，医生说的是她可能再也不能跑，并未让她退学。因此选 B。
questions.passage:
When Jia was twelve, a traffic accident left her with a serious leg injury. Doctors told her she might never run again. For months, she watched her classmates play sports from the sidelines, feeling angry and lonely. Her parents worried that she would give up on exercise completely. Then, during a hospital visit, she met a young athlete who used a running blade — a curved prosthetic leg designed for running. The athlete told Jia that the blade did not make running easy, but it made it possible.

Jia began training slowly, first walking, then jogging short distances with a coach who understood her injury. Progress was painful and uneven. Some days she improved; other days her leg ached and she wanted to quit. Her coach taught her to set small goals: run to the next tree, then to the corner, then around the whole track. Each small goal, once reached, gave her confidence to try the next one. Her classmates, who had once not known what to say to her, began cheering her on during practice.

Two years later, Jia took part in her school's 800-metre race. She did not win, but she finished, and the whole school stood up to applaud. Jia says the race itself was less important than what she learned along the way. She learned that recovery is not a straight line, that asking for help is not a weakness, and that other people's encouragement can make a hard task feel possible. Today, she helps younger students who are recovering from injuries, telling them the same thing the athlete once told her: the equipment does not make it easy, but it can make it possible — and the rest depends on patience and practice.
questions.passage_title: Running With a New Beginning

questions.subject: yingyu
questions.question: What did the young athlete tell Jia about the running blade?
options: It made running easy at once.
It did not make running easy, but it made it possible.
It was only for professional athletes.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到第一段运动员原话——跑步刀片并没有让跑步变得容易，但让跑步成为可能。第一步，A 与原话相反；第二步，C 无依据，文中强调训练是缓慢而痛苦的；第三步，D 是编造，文中没有说只限专业运动员。因此选 B。

questions.subject: yingyu
questions.question: How did Jia's coach help her make progress?
options: By setting small goals, one step at a time.
By telling her to run 800 metres on the first day.
By asking her to train alone without support.
By giving her a new blade every week.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到第二段——教练教她设定小目标：跑到下一棵树，再到拐角，再绕整圈，每个小目标达成后都给她信心尝试下一个。第一步，B 与循序渐进相反；第二步，C 与事实相反，同学和教练都在支持她；第三步，D 是编造，文中没有提到每周换刀片。因此选 A。

questions.question: What happened in Jia's school 800-metre race two years later?
options: She did not win, but she finished and the whole school applauded.
She gave up halfway through the race.
She did not take part in the race.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到第三段——两年后她参加了学校 800 米比赛，没有赢，但跑完了，全校起立鼓掌。第一步，A 与事实相反；第二步，C、D 均与参赛并完赛的事实相反。因此选 B。

questions.question: What does Jia now tell younger students recovering from injuries?
options: Recovery is easy if you have the right equipment.
Asking for help is a weakness.
Equipment can make it possible, but the rest depends on patience and practice.
They should avoid setting small goals.
questions.explanation: 分步解析：定位到最后一段——Jia 现在告诉 younger students 的正是运动员曾告诉她的话：装备并不能让它变容易，但能让它成为可能，其余取决于耐心和练习。第一步，A 与原话相反，装备并不让事情变容易；第二步，B 与原文“寻求帮助不是软弱”相反；第三步，D 与教练的小目标方法相反。因此选 C。
